newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close stronger amid dollar gains.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close stronger amid dollar gains.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger in moderate trade on Friday, benefiting from subdued U.S. economic reports and gains in the Canadian dollar, analysts said.

"The numbers this morning for the U.S. were pretty supportive of the market in general. The market took the revisions to the first-quarter GDP numbers to be positive," said Mark Chandler, senior economist with Goldman Sachs Canada.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.96 to C$112.06 to yield 7.030 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 25/32 to yield 6.91 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to 12 basis points from 11 basis points from the close of trading on Thursday.

Canadian bonds benefited from several U.S. economic reports. Among those was the U.S. Commerce Department's revision of its first-quarter GDP growth estimate to 5.8 percent from 5.6 percent. Economists had forecast growth would be revised upward to 6.0 percent.
"The U.S. market established a bullish back drop, but Canada outperformed in most sectors thanks to month end portfolio indexing," said Technical Data analyst Jeoff Hall.

Canadian bonds were also helped by strength in the Canadian dollar, analysts said. The currency strengthened past C$1.38 (US$0.7246) after Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen told a conference of the world's top currency traders on Friday that prospects were good for a stronger Canadian dollar.
The central bank head said Canada's improved fiscal position, low inflation and a strengthening economy all pointed to an appreciation in the currency.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.50 to C$105.39 to yield 6.508 percent.
The U.S. 10-year bond rose 18/32 to yield 6.66 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds was 15 basis points.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.98 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 4.98 percent.
